newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican sorghum production seen up in Guanajuato.
newsitem.headline: Mexican sorghum production seen up in Guanajuato.

text.p: Mexico's second-largest sorghum producing state, Guanajuato, is expected to boost production to 1.2 million tonnes in the Spring-Summer harvest from 950,000 tonnes in the same-period last year, officials said Monday.
"This year's harvest is looking good, we expect high returns of around 12 tonnes per acre," said Antonio Labourde, director of the Guanajuato Rural and Agricultural Development secretariat.
The secretariat estimated that nationwide sorghum production would hit 5.62 million tonnes this year, making Mexico self-sufficient for the first time in its history.
It said consumption in Mexico was 5.6 million tonnes a year.
Labourde played down the impact of Hurricane Hernan on the state's sorghum harvest last week, saying that weather forecasts were brighter this week.
